extracted.intended_audience: recreational runners and running enthusiasts looking for humorous running puns and jokes
extracted.subtask_description: Creating or selecting short, runner-themed puns and one-liners to amuse runners, ease pre-race nerves, or add light-hearted content to running communities and social posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / use-case of running puns
rubrics_metrics.description: Running puns can come in quite handy to help with pre-race jitters, cheer up a friend, or just remember that running isn’t that serious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use puns as a light-hearted tool: to calm nerves before a race, to cheer up teammates/friends, or to inject levity into running conversations and social feeds. The page frames humor as a way to 'keep running fun' and to remind runners not to take the sport too seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / mechanics of a pun
rubrics_metrics.description: It exploits the different possible meanings of a word or the fact that there are words which sound alike, but have different meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct puns by swapping word meanings or using homophones (sound-alikes). Examples on the page demonstrate this mechanism (e.g., 'I forgot today’s workout. Could you jog my memory?' and 'Why couldn’t the lemon finish the marathon? Because it ran out of juice.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone / expected comedic register
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, I find puns to land in the Dad joke category of a good chuckle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for gentle, groan-inducing humor rather than edgy or highbrow comedy. The target reaction is a light chuckle or smile; acceptability includes cheesiness typical of 'Dad jokes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and formats to use
rubrics_metrics.description: The page presents short one-liners, question-and-answer jokes, knock-knock jokes, and brief funny quotes (e.g., 'Knock, knock… Eyesore who? Eyesore from my long run, can we take the elevator?' and the Jimmy Fallon line: 'How do you know if someone ran a marathon? Don’t worry, they’ll tell you.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor concise formats—single-line puns, Q&A setups, knock-knock structures, and short quoted lines. The article's lists ('Best Running Puns', '25 Best Pun Running Jokes') model these compact forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runner-specific references / vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: So yes, here we’ve got a lot of opportunities to swap words and make all of life just a little bit more about us, runners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor puns in running-specific terms and experiences (pace, marathon, PR, treadmill, pacemaker, calf/calf muscles, souled/sole, gel, courses/trails/tracks). Many examples on the page leverage running vocabulary and race situations to make the wordplay resonate with the running audience.
